theory.intro: To **substitute** is to replace each pronumeral with a given number; to **evaluate** is to work out the result using the order of operations.
facts: **Substitute** by replacing every pronumeral with its value in **brackets**: when $x = 3$, $4x$ becomes $4(3)$.
**Evaluate** using the order of operations — **powers**, then **× and ÷**, then **+ and −**.
In $2x^2$, the power applies to $x$ only: $2x^2=2\times x\times x$. In $(2x)^2$, the brackets make the whole product the number being squared.
The same pronumeral takes the **same value** everywhere it appears.

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate each expression when $x=5$. Show the substitution step.
(a) $7+4x$
(b) $18-3x$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Replace each $x$ with $5$, then multiply before adding or subtracting.
(a) $7+4x$
$=7+4(5)$
$=7+20$
$=27$
(b) $18-3x$
$=18-3(5)$
$=18-15$
$=3$

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate. Show which value replaces each pronumeral.
(a) $\frac{3a+2b}{4}$ when $a=6$ and $b=-1$
(b) $5p+8q-r$ when $p=4$, $q=\frac12$ and $r=7$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Keep the negative value in brackets and work out the whole numerator before dividing.
$\frac{3a+2b}{4}$
$=\frac{3(6)+2(-1)}{4}$
$=\frac{18+(-2)}{4}$
$=\frac{16}{4}$
$=4$
(b) Replace each pronumeral with its own value.
$5p+8q-r$
$=5(4)+8\left(\frac12\right)-(7)$
$=20+4-7$
$=17$

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate both expressions when $x=-4$. Explain why the answers differ.
(a) $2x^2$
(b) $(2x)^2$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Square the value of $x$ before multiplying by $2$.
$2x^2$
$=2(-4)^2$
$=2(16)$
$=32$
(b) The brackets make the whole product $2x$ the number being squared.
$(2x)^2$
$=(2(-4))^2$
$=(-8)^2$
$=64$
The power in (a) applies to $x$ only. In (b), it applies to the whole bracket.
